Do you have automated shutdown for your business why or why not?
i never saw a case that needed automatic shutdown except workstations 10 minutes after work hours, just in case any station is left on.

We have one for the phone lines in our call center if that's what you mean?

in the event of Fire drills and actual emergencies (touch wood) I can call a number which has a trigger to tell all the lines to route calls to emergency closure scripts.

Of course we didn't have it for years until a gas leaked was suspected and no one could get in to the build to shutdown the lines or do it remotely.
Just for when my UPS's runs out which I hope never happens.

No, absolutely not. We toyed with the idea of doing that based on server room tempature for a client, but really we want someone to be able to think and decide before something gets shut off. If theres an error, then we want to know it before we restart.

I guess it would be best to have the automatic shutdown setup for when the UPS runs out as /u/yewbontheboat said, but i never set that up.

We have scripted shutdown procedures to centrally down all Windows and Linux servers, but nothing that will automatically trigger any of them. The scripts must be manually triggered by someone with the right credentials. For the Linux servers, it can only be done by someone who knows how to write a proper for loop in bash.

I get scared just knowing that these scripts exist.

Like others who have posted, we are a 24/7 business. So there is really no way we could just shut down everything. However we do have things like disaster recovery for all our buildings and failovers just in case.

However if we did need to shut down a lot of stuff, we do have a lot of servers hosted virtually so we could in theory just power them all off in some random event.

We have an e-stop/kill switch in each server room. Only a problem severe enough to hit that switch is severe enough to bring everything down.

Think about that; yes, it sucks as much as you imagine. Most individual servers have maintenance windows, some services have maintenance windows. But we're only allowed to take two complete outages a year. Four hours on Christmas eve, and eight hours on New year's eve.
Not an "automated shutdowns" but on the weekends I have 2 of our Windows web hosting servers reboot using Task Scheduler.
